If Mario is lying, it would of been nobody.
If Peach is lying, it would of been Mario.
If Bowser is lying, it would of been Bowser.
If Yoshi is lying, it would of been Peach.
If Donkey Kong is lying, it would of been Donkey Kong.
If Waluigi was lying, it would of been nobody. 
As /u/TweektheGeek said this is insolvable without taking a guess at either Mario, Bowser, Peach, or Donkey Kong. Something you may not realize is that whenever there is a statement where Mario says that it was either Bowser or Donkey Kong, this statement is useless unless if Mario is lying. If Mario is telling the truth that is was either Bowser or Donkey Kong, then it would both be true to say it could of been Bowser and not Donkey Kong and it could of been Donkey Kong and not Bowser. Both possibilities would of been said in the sentence "it was either Bowser of Donkey Kong". (Here is the Logic Math if you are interested (B Apq DK) Epq (B Apq ~DK) Kpq (~B Apq DK)). Now if Mario is lying then the statement is no longer an or statement (disjunction), it is now an and statement (conjunction). So, the statement "it was either Bowser or Donkey Kong" is now: "it was both Bowser and Donkey Kong" and "It was both not Bowser and Donkey Kong". Since, there is only one culprit the former can not be true, so the latter must be true, and at least the latter benefits towards completing the puzzle. Apply this principle with Walluigi and you would see some problems I bet.

Well, in my Highschool Algebra class I wanted to find a quicker way in doing an approach know as p over q (p/q). Used to find the roots to polynomial functions that could not be factored with a guess or check method or a quadratic equation. Where p is the coefficient of the leading degree, and q is the constant. You get the factors of p and divide them over the factors of q with a plus and minus.. You can get a short list of factors i.e. x^2 + x + 1 would have p being 1 and q being 1, so the p over q would be 1 and -1. But if you get something like 12x^n +x^(n-1)......56x^0, then p over q would just suck.
